en: Dependent on a state that is an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is an *āsava*, a state that is not an *āsava* arises by way of the root-condition. Dependent on a state that is an *āsava*, states that are both not an *āsava* and not-not-an-*āsava* arise by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is not an outflow (anāsava), a state that is not an outflow arises by way of the root condition (hetupaccaya).
Dependent on a state that is not an outflow, a state that is not an outflow arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is not an outflow, states that are both not an outflow and not non-outflow arise by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both an *āsava* phenomenon and a non-*āsava* phenomenon, a non-*āsava* phenomenon arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both an *āsava* phenomenon and a non-*āsava* phenomenon, a non-*āsava* phenomenon arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on both an *āsava* phenomenon and a non-*āsava* phenomenon, both non-*āsava* and non-non-*āsava* phenomena arise by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of the cause-condition, there are nine. (In all cases, there are nine.)
